source.place: Lemma 8.3, printed p. 16; the weak-equivalence attachment argument used inside the pushout induction.

proof.text: Consider the square $X\xrightarrow{f}X^{\prime}$ over $\mathrm{id}_A$, with vertical maps $pf$ and $p$. Its canonical comparison to $A\times_A X^{\prime}=X^{\prime}$ is $f$, a weak equivalence by hypothesis. Since $p$ is sharp, the comparison criterion of [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus] makes this square homotopy cartesian. Both vertical maps are sharp by hypothesis. The further base-change clause of that same node therefore says that, for every $t:T\to A$, the actual induced map $X\times_A T\to X^{\prime}\times_A T$ is a weak equivalence. This is an application of the cited statement, not an assertion that arbitrary pullback preserves weak equivalences.

source.place: Lemma 8.3, printed p. 16, last two sentences: base changes of f over A

proof.text: For any $u:U\to B$, give $X$ its map $hpf=qjf=qgi$ to $B$, give $X^{\prime}$ the map $hp=qj$, and put $T=U\times_B A$ with its projection to $A$. Write $Z_U=U\times_B Z$ for each of $Z=X,Y,X^{\prime},Y^{\prime}$. The maps $(x,(v,a))\mapsto(v,x)$ identify $X\times_A T$ with $X_U$ and $X^{\prime}\times_A T$ with $X^{\prime}_U$; the inverse sends $(v,x)$ to $(x,(v,pf(x)))$ in the first case and uses $p(x)$ in the second. These degreewise bijections commute with every simplicial operator and carry the map in step 1 to $f_U=U\times_B f$. Thus $f_U$ is a weak equivalence for every $U\to B$.

source.place: Lemma 8.3, printed p. 16: U times_B f is the base change over U times_B A

proof.text: All four corners of the given pushout have the compatible maps to $B$ just specified. The span is a small diagram in the slice over $B$. By [lem-coef-sset-pullback-preserves-colimits], pulling it back along $U\to B$ gives the pushout $Y^{\prime}_U=Y_U\amalg_{X_U}X^{\prime}_U$, with maps $i_U,f_U,g_U,j_U$. If $i$ is mono, then $i_U$ is mono; if $f$ is mono, then $f_U$ is mono. Indeed a pullback of a degreewise injection is injective: equality of the images of $(v,x_1),(v,x_2)$ forces $x_1=x_2$. No injectivity of $U\to B$ is needed.

source.place: Lemma 8.3, printed p. 16, displayed pulled-back pushout; Proposition 3.7

proof.text: Suppose first that $i$ is mono. Apply the pushout clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] to the map of spans $(X_U\xrightarrow{i_U}Y_U,\ X_U\xrightarrow{1}X_U)\to(X_U\xrightarrow{i_U}Y_U,\ X_U\xrightarrow{f_U}X^{\prime}_U)$ whose components are $(1,1,f_U)$. The designated first legs are $i_U$ in both spans, so both monomorphism hypotheses hold. All three component maps are weak equivalences, by step 2 and the identity axiom of the model structure [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. The first pushout is $Y_U$, the second is $Y^{\prime}_U$ by step 3, and the induced map is precisely $g_U$. Hence $g_U$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 8.3, printed p. 16, left-properness argument when i is mono

proof.text: If instead $f$ is mono, then $f_U$ is both mono and a weak equivalence by steps 2 and 3. In the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], this makes $f_U$ a trivial cofibration, equivalently a member of ${}^{\square}\mathcal F$, where $\mathcal F$ is the class of Kan fibrations (the model lifting and factorization axioms). The pushout-closure clause of [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] gives $g_U\in{}^{\square}\mathcal F$, using the pushout of step 3. Thus $g_U$ is a trivial cofibration and in particular a weak equivalence. This branch requires no monomorphism hypothesis on $i$. Together with step 4, it proves that every $g_U$ is a weak equivalence under the stated disjunction.

source.place: Lemma 8.3, printed p. 16, cofibration pushout argument when f is mono

proof.text: Use the weak-equivalence preservation criterion in [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus] to test $q$. Let $a:U\to V$ be any weak equivalence over $B$. Since $qg$ is sharp, the induced map $a_Y:Y_U\to Y_V$ is a weak equivalence. Let $a_{Y^{\prime}}:Y^{\prime}_U\to Y^{\prime}_V$ be the map to be tested. Naturality of pullback gives $a_{Y^{\prime}}g_U=g_Va_Y$: on a pair $(v,y)$ both composites apply $a$ to the first coordinate and $g$ to the second. Steps 4 and 5 give weak equivalences $g_U,g_V$. Composition and two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] now show that $a_{Y^{\prime}}$ is a weak equivalence. Since $a$ was arbitrary, the cited criterion proves that $q$ is sharp.

title: Sharp pushout attachment comparison
statement: Use small simplicial sets, weak equivalences and monomorphisms of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], sharp maps of [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus], and pushouts of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $i:X\to Y$ and $f:X\to X^{\prime}$ be maps, and let $Y^{\prime}=Y\amalg_X X^{\prime}$ with structure maps $g:Y\to Y^{\prime}$ and $j:X^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$. Let $p:X^{\prime}\to A$, $h:A\to B$ and $q:Y^{\prime}\to B$ satisfy $qj=hp$. Assume $p$, $pf$ and $qg$ are sharp, $f$ is a weak equivalence, and either $i$ or $f$ is a monomorphism. Then $q$ is sharp.
